items.text: Autistic burnout isn't a character flaw. It's a ledger that stopped balancing — too many demands, not enough capacity left to cover them. Math, not morality.
items.rationale: Delivers the core reframe in two short sentences. 'Math, not morality' is the quotable anchor. No advice given; no claim made beyond what the source supports.

items.text: You slept. You took time off. You did everything right. And you still feel broken. That's not failure — rest restores energy. It doesn't rebuild the capacity that masking eroded over years.
items.rationale: Names the specific frustration: doing every recommended thing and still not recovering. Gives it a mechanistic frame (energy vs. capacity) without diagnosing or advising. Speaks to an experience, not the whole community.

items.text: PDA isn't defiance. It's an involuntary threat response — the nervous system firing an alarm it can't override. 'Can't, not won't' isn't a workaround. It's what's actually happening.
items.rationale: Challenges the defiance/manipulation narrative directly using language current in the community. 'Can't, not won't' is the quotable shorthand. No diagnostic claims; frames a mechanism, not a diagnosis.

items.text: Still grieving your late diagnosis months — or years — later? Research tracks this. Identity reconstruction isn't linear, and it doesn't respond to being hurried. You're not behind.
items.rationale: Directly addresses the secondary shame of 'still' grieving, anchored to the 2026 systematic review finding that the process is non-linear by design. 'You're not behind' is the payoff line.

items.text: Unmasking isn't 'just be yourself.' After decades of performing, there's a self to find first. And you mostly find it through other autistic people — not alone in a journal.
items.rationale: Single sharp idea: unmasking is relational, not individual. Pushes back against hollow self-help framing without dismissing it. Speaks to late-diagnosed adults specifically without generalising to all.

items.text: 61% of employers say they're actively recruiting neurodivergent candidates. 42% of neurodivergent employees receive no workplace adjustments at all. What exactly is being supported here?
items.rationale: Juxtaposes the two data points to surface institutional hypocrisy without editorialising. Closing question invites genuine conversation rather than collecting outrage. Stats drawn directly from briefing sources.
items.sensitivity_flag: Verify exact stat figures against the WGU and Simply Psychology sources before posting — numbers drawn from briefing summary, not a direct source read.

items.text: AuDHD/PDA parenting frame: keep the sequence stable (autistic nervous system needs structure for safety) and vary the surface details (ADHD nervous system needs the novelty). Both, not either.
items.rationale: Single actionable frame that names both nervous-system needs without privileging one neurotype over the other. Concrete enough to apply immediately. No rewards/consequences framing that would worsen PDA avoidance.

items.text: ADHD task initiation: the goal isn't to complete the task. Make the first five minutes so small that refusing them feels slightly ridiculous. The nervous system needs a ramp, not a runway.
items.rationale: Reframes the initiation problem in one sentence and gives a one-sentence strategy that works with the neurotype. 'A ramp, not a runway' is the quotable close. No 'this will definitely work for you' overclaim.

items.text: It's not that autistic people 'need control.' There are distinct types of autonomy that create nervous-system safety — sensory, temporal, informational. Knowing which one is under threat changes the whole response.
items.rationale: Moves the conversation from a reductive 'control' framing to a more specific and actionable map of autonomy types. Opens door to self-reflection and practical application for individuals and families alike.
items.sensitivity_flag: Briefing flags this source's publish date as unverified — read the piece before posting to confirm it is current and the autonomy taxonomy is accurately characterised here.

items.text: The demand-avoidant response isn't the enemy. It's a protective part running an old programme — one it learned under real pressure. That's not the same as being broken.
items.rationale: Applies the IFS 'protective part' frame from the Psychology Today May 2026 piece in plain language. Compassionate without being saccharine; gives the avoidance a reason without pathologising the person.

items.text: Autistic burnout tends to hit hardest at transition points — career escalation, becoming a parent, major life change. That's not weakness at the worst moment. It's a nervous system that was already at its limit.
items.rationale: Complements the 'math not morality' reframe by naming specific trigger contexts. Gives people a concrete reason why burnout arrived when it did — reducing self-blame precisely when it's most acute.

items.text: 68% of neurodivergent employees don't know what workplace adjustments they can request. If the company 'supports neurodiversity' but never told you that — what did support actually look like?
items.rationale: Uses the 68% stat to reframe the accommodation gap as an institutional accountability question rather than individual failure. Invites real conversation without targeting individuals. Distinct angle from the 61/42% post.
items.sensitivity_flag: Verify the 68% figure directly against the WGU source before posting.
